name: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) — Annex III evidence
description: Draft projection of EU AI Act obligations for Annex III high-risk ad-targeting decisions (credit, insurance, recruitment) onto the evidence AdCP campaign governance already produces. Arts. 10, 12, and 14 are provider design obligations: a deployer's governance stack can surface evidence for them but does not discharge them. Art. 26 is deployer-side. Prototype of the framework-mapping registry entry format (#3959): not a legal checklist or conformity assessment, with no CI enforcement or PolicyEntry back-references yet.

shared_evidence.description: Check entries on the plan whose policies_evaluated includes the Annex III registry policy.

applies_when_note: Heuristic only, and it can over-include: eu_ai_act_annex_iii also lists pharmaceutical_advertising, which is not an Annex III category. Annex III classification is the deployer's legal determination.

requirements.title: Data and data governance
requirements.requirement_text: Input data used by a high-risk system is subject to data-governance practices, including examination of data for possible biases and handling of special categories of personal data.
requirements.gap_closure: Restricted-attribute screening is evidenced; dataset provenance, quality, and representativeness are not. Closing this needs the agent self-declaration work (Track 2), not a field on the audit log.

requirements.title: Bias examination and mitigation artifacts
requirements.requirement_text: Training, validation, and testing data are examined for biases likely to affect health, safety, or fundamental rights, and appropriate measures are taken to detect, prevent, and mitigate them.
requirements.gap_closure: Bias-testing artifacts come from the provider's model lifecycle and stay out of protocol. A declarative pointer to them could ride on the agent self-declaration work (Track 2).

requirements.title: Automatic recording of events (governance decision log)
requirements.requirement_text: A high-risk system technically allows automatic recording of events (logs) over its lifetime so its operation can be traced.
requirements.gap_closure: Evidences the governance agent's decision log, not the logs of the underlying system. Retention is evidenced separately by Art. 26(6). Requires include_entries: true on get_plan_audit_logs.

requirements.title: Human oversight
requirements.requirement_text: A high-risk system is designed so natural persons can effectively oversee it, including intervening on or overriding its output.
requirements.gap_closure: A plan with human_review_required: true obliges the governance agent to escalate every action, so every check entry must show a reviewer and run in enforce mode; one unreviewed or audit-mode check drops the row to partial. human_review_required lives on the plan, not on get_plan_audit_logs, so it needs the hash-matched plan supplement. Reviewer competence and the review workflow are outside the protocol.

requirements.title: Awareness of automation bias
requirements.requirement_text: Persons assigned to oversight remain aware of the tendency to over-rely on the system's output.
requirements.gap_closure: The escalation rate is a proxy for whether overseers stay engaged, not evidence of their awareness of automation bias, and the threshold is operator-configured (a minimum of 0 passes trivially). The row stays partial; going further needs a human-factors attestation outside the protocol.

requirements.title: Deployer log retention
requirements.requirement_text: Deployers keep the logs automatically generated by the high-risk system, to the extent under their control, for a period appropriate to the intended purpose and at least six months.
requirements.gap_closure: get_plan_audit_logs carries no retention period or chain-of-custody guarantee. A retention statement supplied by the exporting operator is an assertion, not protocol evidence, so this row cannot exceed partial until a governance agent can state retention on the wire.
